item.title: OSRD vs OpenRailwayMap vs Open Rails in 2026: Self-Hosting a Railway Planning, Mapping and Simulation Stack
item.description: Railway engineering has one of the worst open-source toolchains of any infrastructure discipline. Signalling layouts live in proprietary CAD formats, capacity studies are done in vendor software that costs more per seat than a car, and the schedule data your national operator publishes is a PDF. The result is that a small but genuinely useful stack of open tools goes almost completely unnoticed outside a handful of national railway labs.
